description: Shared environment style guide for authored environment assets in Ascension, split by HQ and raid base-map surface.
principles: HQ and raids are separate visual surfaces and should not be forced into one environment grammar.
HQ environments should read as compact inhabitable spaces, not abstract diagrams.
Raid base maps should read as flat top-down exploration surfaces first, not as perspective rooms.
Reusable parts exist to support composition, not to replace composition.
Each surface should optimize for its own readability contract.

hq: Use an angled/isometric room box with visible floor depth and enclosing wall planes.
HQ room kits must share one canonical module footprint and grid so adjacent rooms snap together cleanly.
Use layered ownership: shell/perimeter, structure, room recipe, props, and theme.
Doors, windows, and thresholds should read as openings in architecture rather than pasted icons.
Props should imply circulation, occupancy, and room function.
raidBaseMap: Use a flat top-down minimap language for tiles, chambers, corridors, fog, and feature markers.
Optimize for exploration readability and moving team dots over environmental illusion.
Base raid-map assets must not depend on isometric room-box geometry.
Enemy, team, and feature visuals should remain lightweight at base zoom.

doNotUse: flat top-down diagrams as approved HQ room scenes
pure side elevations as approved HQ room scenes
simple wall-slice cross-sections as approved HQ room scenes
standalone HQ room dioramas that cannot tile with adjacent rooms
stacking multiple full room-scene SVGs that each own their own walls and floor planes into one HQ layout
HQ isometric room-box geometry for the raid base map
